X-Forwarded-For.title: Forwarded client addresses and trusted proxy context
X-Forwarded-For.description: Forwarded client-address metadata describes an earlier request path only when interpreted through trusted proxy context, separately from the origin’s actual socket peer.

XMLTV.title: XMLTV listings: channels, programmes and time
XMLTV.description: XMLTV represents channel identities and programme listings in XML, with format-specific timestamps and episode-number systems that a guide importer must interpret.

XMP.title: XMP metadata
XMP.description: XMP defines an extensible metadata model and RDF/XML serialization whose namespaced properties can be embedded in resources or carried in associated sidecars.

adaptive bitrate streaming.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming and representation selection
adaptive bitrate streaming.description: Adaptive bitrate streaming selects among suitable representations of the same programme timeline to balance presentation quality, delivery capacity and playback reserve.

audio clipping.title: Audio Clipping
audio clipping.description: Clipping occurs when a signal exceeds a stage’s available range and its peaks are limited.

audio dithering.title: Audio Dithering
audio dithering.description: Dither adds a small controlled noise signal before quantization to avoid signal-dependent rounding distortion.

automatic brightness limiting.title: Automatic brightness limiting
automatic brightness limiting.description: Automatic brightness limiting reduces permitted display output as picture loading reaches the implementation’s power or drive constraints.

binaural.title: Binaural Audio
binaural.description: Binaural audio supplies left-ear and right-ear signals with the cues used to perceive sound direction.

black-frame insertion.title: Black-frame insertion and display persistence
black-frame insertion.description: Black-frame insertion or timed dark intervals reduce visible picture persistence by interrupting illumination between presentations.

broadcast multiplex.title: Broadcast multiplexes
broadcast multiplex.description: A broadcast multiplex combines several service/component data streams into one defined transport/acquisition context, with shared capacity and signaling linking the selected programme to its packets.

bufferbloat.title: Bufferbloat and standing queue delay
bufferbloat.description: Bufferbloat is excessive standing queue delay under load, where retained work can keep link utilization high while delaying interactive and media-control traffic.

chase playback.title: Chase playback while a recording grows
chase playback.description: Chase playback reads an ongoing recording before capture finishes, coordinating a growing usable endpoint with the reader’s position and the recording’s final completion state.

codec level.title: Video Codec Levels and Tiers
codec level.description: Codec levels and tiers describe resource limits that a compatible decoder must satisfy.

codec profile.title: Video Codec Profiles
codec profile.description: A video codec profile constrains the coding tools and sample formats a stream may use.

constant rate factor.title: Constant Rate Factor (CRF) for Video
constant rate factor.description: Constant rate factor is an encoder-specific quality control that produces variable bitrate without targeting an exact output size.

copy back video.title: Copy-back video pipelines
copy back video.description: A copy-back video path makes hardware-decoded pictures available in a CPU-oriented representation so software consumers can process them before later delivery or encoding.

copy-back video.title: Copy-back video pipelines
copy-back video.description: A copy-back video path makes hardware-decoded pictures available in a CPU-oriented representation so software consumers can process them before later delivery or encoding.

deinterlacing.title: Deinterlacing
deinterlacing.description: Deinterlacing reconstructs complete display pictures from an interlaced video's alternating fields.

dialnorm.title: Dialogue normalization (dialnorm)
dialnorm.description: Dialnorm metadata describes a Dolby programme's dialogue reference level so the reproduction system can choose a corresponding gain.

double NAT.title: Double NAT and two translation boundaries
double NAT.description: Double NAT places two translation boundaries in a connection path, requiring their endpoint mappings and state to compose before outside traffic can reach an internal server.

eARC.title: HDMI Enhanced Audio Return Channel (eARC)
eARC.description: Enhanced Audio Return Channel expands the supported TV-to-audio-system transport and capability relationship beyond conventional ARC.

fMP4.title: Fragmented MP4
fMP4.description: Fragmented MP4 distributes timing and sample descriptions across successive media fragments after an initial track description.

field order.title: Video Field Order
field order.description: Field order identifies which set of alternating picture lines comes first in time.

file stacking.title: Multipart movies and file stacking
file stacking.description: A multipart movie divides one intended feature across sequential resources whose local timelines must be interpreted as parts of a whole.

filter graph.title: Media filter graphs
filter graph.description: A media filter graph connects decoded-frame transformations through defined input/output relationships whose order, format and branching affect the result.

filtergraph.title: Media filter graphs
filtergraph.description: A media filter graph connects decoded-frame transformations through defined input/output relationships whose order, format and branching affect the result.

group of pictures.title: Groups of Pictures (GOPs)
group of pictures.description: A group of pictures describes a sequence of coded pictures and their prediction relationships around access points.

hairpin NAT.title: NAT loopback and same-network public endpoints
hairpin NAT.description: NAT loopback lets an inside client use an outside mapped endpoint for an inside service, with compatible translation and return routing keeping the client’s expected peer consistent.

inter-frame prediction.title: Inter-Frame Video Prediction
inter-frame prediction.description: Inter-frame prediction reconstructs a picture using previously decoded reference pictures and coded corrections.

interlaced video.title: Interlaced Video
interlaced video.description: Interlaced video records alternating sets of picture lines as fields captured at successive times.

intra-frame compression.title: Intra-Frame Video Compression
intra-frame compression.description: Intra-frame compression represents a picture using information from within that picture rather than other pictures.

inverse telecine.title: Inverse Telecine
inverse telecine.description: Inverse telecine reconstructs progressive film pictures from a telecined television cadence.

keyframe.title: Video Keyframes and Random Access
keyframe.description: A video random-access point lets decoding begin without reconstructing the whole preceding stream.

local dimming.title: Local dimming and backlight zones
local dimming.description: Local dimming adjusts illumination in backlight regions so an LCD can use different light levels across the same picture.

loopback address.title: Loopback addresses and the meaning of localhost
loopback address.description: Loopback addresses reach the requesting host’s own network stack, making localhost useful for same-host access while proving little about another device’s server path.

mDNS.title: Multicast DNS and local-link naming
mDNS.description: Multicast DNS resolves specified names on a local link through participating responders, with DNS-based service discovery adding service-instance and endpoint information.

matrix surround.title: Matrix Surround
matrix surround.description: Matrix surround encodes spatial relationships into fewer channels for later surround decoding.

mixed content.title: Mixed content and a browser’s secure-page boundary
mixed content.description: Mixed-content processing governs insecure subrequests made by a secure browser page, with request type, upgrade policy and local-network features separate from CORS and server reachability.

motion interpolation.title: Motion Interpolation
motion interpolation.description: Motion interpolation estimates new pictures between existing video frames to create a smoother presentation.

nit.title: Luminance and Nits
nit.description: A nit is one candela per square metre, a unit used to describe the luminance of displayed images.

nits.title: Luminance and Nits
nits.description: A nit is one candela per square metre, a unit used to describe the luminance of displayed images.

object-based audio.title: Object-Based Audio
object-based audio.description: Object-based audio combines sound components with metadata that a renderer uses to place them for the listening system.

oneVPL.title: Intel VPL and the oneVPL name
oneVPL.description: Intel VPL is the media library interface and dispatcher used to select supported Intel video implementations and coordinate decode, encode and processing sessions.

pixel aspect ratio.title: Video Pixel Aspect Ratio
pixel aspect ratio.description: Pixel aspect ratio describes how wide each video sample is intended to appear relative to its height.

progressive video.title: Progressive Video
progressive video.description: Progressive video represents each picture as a complete frame rather than fields from successive capture times.

quantization parameter.title: Video Quantization Parameter (QP)
quantization parameter.description: A quantization parameter selects quantization strength in a video coding process and is not a universal picture-quality score.

reference frames.title: Video Reference Frames
reference frames.description: Reference frames are decoded pictures retained so that other pictures can use them for prediction.

remux.title: Remuxing media containers
remux.description: Remuxing places existing encoded streams into another container or delivery package without re-encoding those streams.

remuxing.title: Remuxing media containers
remuxing.description: Remuxing places existing encoded streams into another container or delivery package without re-encoding those streams.

reverse proxy.title: Reverse proxies and the two-sided server path
reverse proxy.description: A reverse proxy accepts a public-facing application request and makes a separate upstream request, translating endpoint and resource context according to its configured policy.

split DNS.title: Split DNS and location-dependent server endpoints
split DNS.description: Split DNS supplies different answers for a name under different resolver views, allowing one server hostname to select local and external endpoints without changing its other URL components.

split tunneling.title: VPN routing, overlapping prefixes and split tunneling
split tunneling.description: VPN routing determines which destination prefixes use a tunnel, with route specificity, overlapping address realms and DNS policy separate from the tunnel’s connected state.

stream copy.title: Stream copying and encoded packet handling
stream copy.description: Stream copying passes selected encoded stream data to an output path without decoding and re-encoding its pictures or samples.

streamcopy.title: Stream copying and encoded packet handling
streamcopy.description: Stream copying passes selected encoded stream data to an output path without decoding and re-encoding its pictures or samples.

structural similarity.title: Structural Similarity (SSIM) for Video
structural similarity.description: SSIM compares local luminance, contrast, and structure between decoded pictures and a reference.

telecine.title: Telecine and 3:2 Pulldown
telecine.description: 3:2 pulldown distributes film pictures over alternating two-field and three-field intervals for television presentation.

time-shift buffer.title: Time-shift buffers and the retained live window
time-shift buffer.description: A time-shift buffer retains a bounded portion of an advancing live stream so playback can pause or rewind within media that has not yet been evicted.

transcode throttling.title: Transcode throttling and producer lead
transcode throttling.description: Transcode throttling limits work produced ahead of playback by pausing or reducing a producer whose output lead is already sufficient.

transmuxing.title: Remuxing media containers
transmuxing.description: Remuxing places existing encoded streams into another container or delivery package without re-encoding those streams.

two-pass encoding.title: Two-Pass Video Encoding
two-pass encoding.description: Two-pass video encoding analyzes a source before a final encode so the encoder can allocate an overall bitrate budget across it.

tx3g.title: MP4 timed text (tx3g)
tx3g.description: tx3g identifies a 3GPP timed-text sample entry whose container timing and text modifiers describe a subtitle track.

variable frame rate.title: Variable Frame Rate
variable frame rate.description: Variable frame rate allows the interval between successive video pictures to change.

variable refresh rate.title: Variable refresh rate (VRR)
variable refresh rate.description: Variable refresh rate allows a supported display route to vary presentation intervals within a defined operating range.

virtual surround.title: Virtual Surround
virtual surround.description: Virtual surround uses signal processing to suggest spatial positions with fewer physical speakers or with headphones.

x86-64.title: x86-64 architecture and compatible server software
x86-64.description: x86-64 is a 64-bit processor architecture used by common server packages, but software also needs a matching operating system, ABI and instruction support.

xHE-AAC.title: xHE-AAC Audio
xHE-AAC.description: xHE-AAC combines Extended HE-AAC based on USAC with MPEG-D loudness and dynamic-range control for speech and music delivery.

xmltv_ns.title: XMLTV listings: channels, programmes and time
xmltv_ns.description: XMLTV represents channel identities and programme listings in XML, with format-specific timestamps and episode-number systems that a guide importer must interpret.

zero copy video.title: Zero-copy video pipelines and the boundary being avoided
zero copy video.description: A zero-copy claim identifies a picture handoff that avoids a particular data copy, while compatible storage, processing and synchronization determine the remaining pipeline traffic.

zero-copy video.title: Zero-copy video pipelines and the boundary being avoided
zero-copy video.description: A zero-copy claim identifies a picture handoff that avoids a particular data copy, while compatible storage, processing and synchronization determine the remaining pipeline traffic.
